responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for Synopsys ARC processors, covering how generic GCC code is configured, lowered, optimized, and emitted for ARC architecture families and operating environments. Its core arc.cc/arc.c, arc.h, and arc.md files implement ARC target hooks, ABI and calling-convention policy, operand and address legitimacy, prologue/epilogue generation, atomics, builtins, delay-slot and conditional-execution handling, instruction costs, and final assembly output, while the ARC option and CPU-description tables (arc.opt, arc-options.def, arc-cpus.def, arc-arch.h, generated option fragments, and driver-arc) define selectable CPUs, architectural feature combinations, tuning, and assembler-driver mapping. The machine-description subfiles split out major ARC instruction-set areas such as core constraints and predicates, scheduler models for ARC600/700/EM/HS families, atomic operations, SIMD/vector support, and older FPX versus newer hardware FPU support, and the C-family builtin hook plus builtins/intrinsic headers provide ARC-specific preprocessor macros and user-visible builtins. Subtarget headers like elf.h, linux.h, and big.h adapt the common ARC backend to bare-metal, Linux, and endianness-specific runtime conventions, making this module the place where ARC-specific ISA, microarchitecture, ABI, and toolchain behavior are integrated into GCC.
